newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends up on central bank support.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends up on central bank support.

text.p: The won closed stronger versus the dollar on Thursday on the back of firm support by the central Bank of Korea, traders said.
The central bank started selling dollars at the opening to slow the won's fall, they said. But the bank denied the move as it regularly does.
The won closed at 867.50 after opening at an intraday low of 870.00. It peaked at 866.10.
"The central bank stepped in to put a stop to speculative dollar buying," said one local dealer.
Many banks have been accumulating dollars on speculation that the won would fall, traders said. Growing import deals have also pressured the local unit.
The base mid-rate is seen at 867.80 for Monday, compared with 869.90 for Thursday. The market will be closed on Friday due to the Lunar New Year holiday.
